articles.title: Pepelu: "Sadiq es el caos en persona, una caja de sorpresas, como el gol que ha marcado"
articles.standfirst: El jugador del Valencia, que volvió a actuar como central, valora la importancia del triunfo ante el Elche antes de la visita del Real madrid
articles.summary: El jugador del Valencia, que volvió a actuar como central, valora la importancia del triunfo ante el Elche antes de la visita del Real madrid
articles.body: Tras la victoria del Valencia ante el Elche en el Martínez Valero, la expedición blanquinegra estaba muy feliz por el triunfo y por el protagonismo de Sadiq, un compañero muy querido en el vestuario que había pasado dos meses lesionados. Pepelu destacó el impacto del atacante en una acción que definió como muy representativa de su personalidad futbolística. "Es un gol muy de Sadiq. Es el caos en persona, una caja de sorpresas", afirmó el centrocampista valencianista en la zona mixta del estadio ilicitano. El jugador de Dénia también subrayó la importancia de un triunfo que considera un alivio para el vestuario y aseguró que el equipo afronta con más confianza la visita del Real Madrid a Mestalla. ¿Era muy necesaria esta victoria para el vestuario? "Sí, la verdad es que sí. Estamos muy contentos porque, con la llegada del míster, es verdad que no habíamos conseguido buenas sensaciones, pero creo que esta victoria es un alivio para todos: para ellos, para nosotros y para la afición. Es un paso importante". ¿Qué ha pensado en esa última acción, en el último remate del Elche? "Se me ha pasado de todo por la cabeza, pero creo que al final el fútbol es justo. El otro día se nos escapó el partido en la última jugada. Hoy me alegro mucho por Stole Dimitrievski, por esa parada, porque nos ha dado la victoria y, sobre todo, estoy contento por nosotros". ¿Cómo se encuentra jugando de central, una posición en la que está actuando últimamente? "Bien. Siempre lo he dicho: donde me ponga el míster, lo importante es el equipo. Hemos conseguido volver a ganar y me quedo con eso y con las buenas sensaciones". ¿Esta victoria da más confianza para intentar ganar al Madrid la semana que viene? "Sí, mucho más. Al final, crecer desde la victoria da mucha confianza. Ahora llega el Madrid, pero sabemos que en Mestalla no hay imposibles y ojalá podamos brindarle a la afición la primera victoria". ¿Cómo ha visto el gol de Sadiq? Parecía que marcaba, que no, que sí... ¿Cómo lo ha vivido? "Es un gol muy de Sadiq, la verdad. No tengo que decir nada. Como he dicho antes, es el caos en persona, una caja de sorpresas. Me alegro porque ha vuelto después de mucho tiempo y, además, es un gol que nos da la victoria". ¿La asignatura pendiente es ahora ganar en casa, en Mestalla? "Sí. Llevamos varios partidos sin conseguirlo. El equipo lo quiere y lo busca. Dar ese golpe para brindar una alegría a la afición es lo que queremos todos". ¿Se puede ganar al Madrid en Mestalla el próximo sábado? "Sí, por supuesto. Ya lo hemos hecho. Al menos desde que estoy aquí, le he ganado al Madrid y ojalá el sábado podamos conseguir otra victoria, porque sería el colofón antes del parón".

articles.summary: Dos tantos de Alajbegovic y Boga en la recta final decidieron el choque
articles.body: Luciano Spalletti siempre será recordado como un mito en el Maradona. Ahora bien, se jugaba su continuidad al frente de la Juventus y, gracias a dos 'zapatazos' de Alajbegovic y Boga el tramo final de partido, consiguió coger algo de oxígeno... a consta de un Nápoles (2-0) que se queda a seis puntos de los puestos europeos que marca el sorprendente Frosinone. La última derrota contra el Genoa provocó que Spalletti aboliese la línea de tres por la que venía abogando en la Juventus durante las últimas fechas. Sí mantuvo, sin embargo, la doble punta formada por Kolo Muani y Woltemade. Allegri, que vio el partido desde el palco por sanción, le dio al alternativa a Marianucci en el eje de la zaga y ubicó a Lucca en punta por la ausencia de Hojlund. El Nápoles trató de sacarle rédito a la presencia del espigado ariete italiano. A los siete minutos, de hecho, conectó un centro lateral de Politano que Vicario sacó de forma brillante. No fue el único susto que se llevó la Juventus en los primeros compases. Y es que, en su intento por robar de espaldas, Koopmeiners se jugó la roja por un 'pisotón' sobre Anguissa. Se respiraba cierta calma tensa. Douglas Luíz y Lucumí, de hecho, fueron amonestados a las primeras de cambio. La Juventus, sin embargo, trató de asentarse con alguna secuencia más larga con balón. Woltemade, aunque bastante forzado, tuvo la primera en el 19' rematando un centro lateral de Alajbegovic desde el costado izquierdo. Más claro fue el de Cabal al larguero en el 28' a la salida de un córner. El colombiano, además, reclamó un penalti de Olivera. Ambos equipos se dieron un pequeño respiro hasta el descanso. Sin embargo, quien parecía que empezaba a hacer la guerra por su cuenta era un Kerim Alajbegovic que se sacó un 'zurdazo' en la última jugada de la primera parte que Meret sacó con apuros para conservar el 0-0 en el marcador. La entrada de Gatti en la Juventus y Rrahamani y Gilmour en el Nápoles modificó la estructura de ambas 'squadras'. Fueron, de hecho, ajustes eminentemente conservadores. Antes de llegar a la hora de encuentro, por si fuera poco, Spalletti volvió a intervenir. Reclamó los servicios de Zhegrova y retiró a un Kolo Muani que volvió a firmar otro partido tremendamente gris. Se quedó Woltemade como única referencia. Como respuesta, Landucci sacó al campo a Vergara. En total, cinco cambios en un cuarto de hora. Se terminó de instalar el miedo a poder perder y marcharse de vacío. Pero, a falta de 20' para el final, Alajbegovic hizo saltar todo por los aires justo antes de abandonar el terreno de juego. Recibió de Zhegrova, que desatascó la acción, y conectó un 'zurdazo' que tocó en la madera antes de superar a Meret. Poco a poco, empieza a carburar el bosnio: suma dos goles y una asistencia. Se le ponía cuesta arriba el encuentro a un Nápoles inofensivo. Por si fuera poco, Marianucci vio la segunda amarilla cinco minutos después de encajar el 1-0 y terminaron de firmar su sentencia con el tanto de Boga, también desde fuera del área, en el 85'. Ambos necesitaban la victoria... y se la acabó llevando una Juventus que, en cualquier caso, todavía se mantiene a tres puntos de Europa.

articles.title: ¡Qué porterazo tiene el Athletic!
articles.standfirst: Simón asegura la victoria en un derbi en el que la Real protestó mucho el penalti del 2-1
articles.summary: Simón asegura la victoria en un derbi en el que la Real protestó mucho el penalti del 2-1
articles.body: Dicen que los derbis son esos partidos en los que no vale la clasificación. Dicen que la historia no sabe del momento. También dicen que lo único que cuenta es la buena sensación y el aquí y ahora. Ese compendio de hilos que conforman la madeja de un partido determinó que el cruce de San Mamés fuera para el Athletic, que hizo buena su victoria del pasado domingo frente al Getafe y el estado de nirvana emocional en el que vive con la designación de Simón como el mejor portero del mundo. También hizo bueno que a Terzic se le dé bien Matarazzo, al que ha ganado casi todas las veces en las que se han enfrentado. El alemán ha entrado con buen pie en estas batallas de comunidad y el resultado de San Mamés permite al Athletic regresar a las victorias después de tres derbis consecutivos sin hacerlo. Lo descrito en las pizarras de cada vestuario quedó en papel mojado al poco de superarse el primer minuto. Iñaki Williams bajó hasta el medio campo para recibir un pase por bajo de Simón y abrirlo de la misma a su hermano Nico, que después de avanzar por su costado envió el balón al otro lado. Por allí apareció Rincón para colocar el balón el el corazón del área. Berenguer remató casi sin querer a medio metro de la línea de gol y la mandó fuera. El navarro la golpeó de manera precipitada porque por delante de él volaron Maroan y Sarr. No fue sólo que ahí estuvo el 1-0, sino que Sarr cayó sobre la pierna de Maroan, que al instante tuvo que pedir el cambio y dejó el campo entre lágrimas por su mala suerte. El contratiempo no cortó el fuego de un Athletic que continuó apretando por tomar una ventaja que llegó en el minuto 14 con gol de Iñaki Williams tras correr al espacio a un buen balón servido por su hermano. No fue hasta el 1-0 cuando la Real pudo soltarse un poco y cruzar más de dos pases en el campo del Athletic, aunque el conjunto txuriurdin continuó sufriendo. Robert Navarro y Berenguer dispusieron de dos buenos remates para aumentar la renta, pero los dos intentos se fueron muy desviados. La Real quiso crecer a partir de la posesión, que era la manera de relajar la tensión que le interesaba mantener al Athletic, y se metió de lleno en el encuentro con un zapatazo de Sucic que quedará como el primer gol encajado por Simón tras ser elegido mejor portero del mundo. El portero estuvo soberbio cuando menos de cinco minutos más tarde desvió a córner un remate a corta distancia de Barrene. La Real se había subido ya al mismo nivel que marcaba el Athletic. En el 38’ el portero brilló otra vez para enviar a córner un remate de Oyarzabal, pero todo se volteó de nuevo cuando en el 45’ Hernández Hernández fue derecho al punto de penalti tras una disputa de Aramburu con Nico que Berenguer convirtió en gol con suspense, pues pasó por debajo del cuerpo de Remiro. La Real se quejó del penalti hasta el pitido final. En un San Mamés con la mejor asistencia de la temporada -la primera vez del curso que se superó los 50.000 espectadores- el segundo periodo arrancó con una chispa magnífica que aceleraba las idas y venidas, con alternativas en los dos lados del campo. En el 55’ los hinchas de la Real quisieron cobrarse el penalti del primer tiempo en una acción entre Guedes y Yuri que Hernández Hernández no consideró y tampoco lo hicieron desde el VAR. La pasión fue dejando paso a una aportación más quirúrgica en el juego de cada uno de los equipos. La asumible pérdida de energía iba a dar paso a otro quehacer en la búsqueda de un gol para la Real que el Athletic pretendía a partir del contragolpe o una salida más vertical. Y es que el balón en el último tramo del choque fue más txuriurdin que rojiblanco. Pero en este tiempo la Real no contó con las ocasiones que sí había sumado cuando todavía no se había dado el cambio de campo. Si la Real no empató fue porque Simón, otra vez Simón, tiró de guante de oro ante Soler. El valenciano tuvo luego otra opción con un remate desde dentro del área que fue catastrófico. Esa acción se dio con el Athletic con 10 futbolistas ya que Hernández Hernández retrasó un minuto la entrada al campo de Prados porque Canales, al que iba a sustituir, demoró su salida del terreno de juego.

articles.title: Aramburu: "Toco balón, me parece increíble que pite penalti, hasta Nico me dice que no es"
articles.standfirst: El defensa de la Real se mostró indignado con la decisión del árbitro en la acción que protagonizó con Nico Williams y que terminó decidiendo el derbi
articles.summary: El defensa de la Real se mostró indignado con la decisión del árbitro en la acción que protagonizó con Nico Williams y que terminó decidiendo el derbi
articles.body: Jon Mikel Aramburu no dio crédito en directo sobre el césped de San Mamés a que Hernández Hernández señalase penalti suyo sobre Nico Williams, en una acción que terminó decidiendo el derbi, porque tenía claro que tocó el balón, como así corroboró al final del partido cuando le enseñaron la imagen en televisión. Aramburu fue preguntado al final del partido en Dazn por lo disputado del derbi. “Todos los derbis son disputados y sabíamos que iba a ser así y que se iba decidir por detalles y ha sido con un penalti que no lo es. Me acaban de enseñar que el chip que dice claramente que toco el balón y el árbitro afirma que yo no toco el balón, teniendo la tecnología me parece increíble que pite un penalti así, cuando claramente toco el balón, hasta Nico me decía que para él no era penalti, es una pena que el derbi se haya decidido por una acción polémica”. Le insistieron en esa jugada decisiva y en lo que le había dicho el jugador del Athletic, y el realista siguió reclamando su inocencia. “Sí, que el toque era mínimo, que yo había tocado el balón, eso le decía yo a Nico y el árbitro me dice que es penalti confirmado porque en el VAR me han dicho que no tocas el balón e insisto en que em acaban de enseñar la jugada con el chip en la televisión donde claramente toco el balón, así que es una injusticia lo que ha pasado”. Aramburu estaba visiblemente enojado. “Claro que estamos enfadados, porque pensamos que hemos sido perjudicados por esa acción, a ver que dice el árbitro ahora cuando hable. Además, Unai Simón ha demostrado el porqué del trofeo que ganó, porque hizo un partidazo”.

articles.title: El gesto de Diomande con el que se ganó a El Sardinero
articles.standfirst: Gran ovación al ser sustituido por regalar su camiseta a un chaval
articles.summary: Gran ovación al ser sustituido por regalar su camiseta a un chaval
articles.body: En el minuto 85 de partido, el ambiente en El Sardinero saturaba decibelios. Se mezclaban el enfado monumental de la afición del Racing con Munuera Montero y el agradecimiento a su equipo por no dejarse llevar hacia una goleada escandalosa tras el 0-3 al descanso. Entonces se paró el partido para la que iba a ser la última sustitución. Desde el banquillo del Madrid se levantó el luminoso con el 25 para que saliera Diomande del campo y entrara Endrick. Colocado en su banda, la contraria a la de las sustituciones, Diomande no cruzó el terreno de juego. Con 0-3 en el marcador, decidió salir por su banda y recorrer el perímetro del campo por fuera para dirigirse al vestuario. De repente, y en medio de la histeria que rodeaba al partido, una ovación comenzó a acompañar el camino del delantero del Madrid hacia los vestuarios. ¿Qué había pasado? ¿Por qué el costamarfileño caminaba sin camiseta? La respuesta estaba en la grada que ocupan los chavales de la cantera del Racing y en la camiseta del jugador del Madrid que sostenía uno de ellos. Ese chico de las categorías inferiores del Racing comenzó a gritar cuando se realizó el cambio: "¡Diomande, dame tu camiseta! ¡Diomande, dame tu camiseta!". Al principio, el jugador del Madrid pasó de largo, como si no hubiera entendido nada. De repente, se quedó parado, dio media vuelta y buscó al muchacho que se desgañitaba pidiendo la camiseta. Se fue hasta la zona que ocupaba, en la primera fila de la tribuna contraria al palco, y se la dio. A la alegría del chico, que abrazaba su tesoro, se sumó toda la gran ovación dedicada a Diomande por ese sector del estadio. Los que lo vieron y aquellos a los que les fueron contando qué había pasado fueron los protagonistas de una ovación que sonaba fuera de lugar en el tenso contexto del partido.

articles.title: Terzic: "Estamos en el buen camino"
articles.standfirst: El técnico rojiblanco trabaja ahora por extender más tiempo el mejor rendimiento del equipo
articles.summary: El técnico rojiblanco trabaja ahora por extender más tiempo el mejor rendimiento del equipo
articles.body: El triunfo en el derbi refuerzas las sensaciones del Athletic y deja satisfecho a Terzic. "Estamos muy contentos con la victoria. El mensaje es que estamos en buen camino. Los primeros treinta minutos han sido increíbles por cómo hemos presionado y ha habido oportunidades. El trabajo es ampliar estos 30 minutos y conseguir que el rendimiento se vaya hasta los minutos", expresó. El partido de Simón: "Unai ha demostrado por qué es el mejor portero del mundo. La Real marcó en su primera oportunidad y luego Unai nos salvó y dio estabilidad, pero muchos jugadores han rendido muy bien para que este triunfo sucediera. La jugada del penalti: "Hay que recordar lo que dije otras veces. Ha habido decisiones duras en nuestra contra otras veces y nunca he dicho nada al respecto. Tampoco lo haré ahora porque no me gusta hablar de los árbirros, ni de buena ni de mala manera". La importancia del triunfo: "Estoy totalmente de acuerdo. Tenemos que subir en la clasificación porque necesitamos puntos y la Real es un rival muy complicado porque venía de cuatro victorias consecutivas. La lesión de Maroan: "Sintió un tirón en los isquios al poco de empezar. Ha sido una mala situación para él. Después del partido estaba algo más optimista respecto a su estado físico. Con Maroan jugamos con dos delanteros centros. Cruzamos los dedos con lo que pueda tener. Esperamos conocer algo más en uno o dos días".

articles.title: After firing Mike Norvell, here comes the hard part for Florida State: Finding a coach who wants the job
articles.summary: FSU's decision to end the Norvell era will provide relief for a fan base that simply had enough. But Seminole fans should also prepare for a dose of humility...
articles.body:
The last time Florida State went looking for a football coach, it was widely considered among the best 15 jobs in the sport.

The list of big names associated with the job was long, encompassing everyone from Lane Kiffin to James Franklin. And when Florida State's search locked in on Mike Norvell, who had just taken Memphis to the Cotton Bowl, it needed to beat out other prominent schools like Arkansas and Ole Miss who had significant interest in him.

That's how enduring the Florida State brand was, even after the messy exit of Jimbo Fisher to Texas A&M and the woebegone Willie Taggart era had left the program in tatters. It was still viewed as a place the right coach could come in and contend for national titles.

But with that same coaching search taking place today, it's difficult to see how Florida State is in position to land the hottest young coach in the country or beat out even the lower-level SEC schools. As college football has evolved in the seven years since hiring Norvell, Florida State enters the coaching market today dealing with a new reality it hasn't experienced since Bobby Bowden brought the program to greatness.

As the school will learn in the coming days and weeks, it's just not considered an elite job anymore.

To be sure, Florida State's decision to end the Norvell era following Saturday's awful 36-24 loss at home to Clemson will provide relief for a fan base that simply had enough. Even if you believe Norvell to be a quality coach who was the victim of unfortunate circumstances, his tenure was unrecoverable after losing 21 out of his last 26 games against power conference opponents.

It should never get that bad in Tallahassee, and the next coach will undoubtedly benefit from the simple act of turning the page.

But Florida State fans should also prepare for a dose of humility as speculation about their candidate pool gets underway. While the timing of this change could be fortuitous for the Seminoles — the lack of competition on the job market so far will create favorable conditions for a good hire — there are a number of factors that add up to a reality many Florida State fans may not be ready for.

The candidate pool this time will not look as attractive on the surface as it was during their previous two searches. Among the reasons for that, according to industry sources who have planned on the FSU job coming open this year, is financial issues.

Florida State is, for lack of a better term, kind of broke

One of the reasons why Norvell's tenure blew up so spectacularly is that Florida State, according to sources, fell into the middle of the pack of the ACC in terms of roster spending despite early success in the transfer portal.

"Norvell embraced the portal because that's the only way to get players in and try to flip it right away and they got a lot of those players," one person familiar with the situation told Yahoo Sports. "They had money. They might have had like $8 million in the first or second rev-share years, which would have been top 15 or top 20 and they just didn't keep pace with it. The last three years, they've been really behind."

Some will argue that Florida State's boosters stopped giving money because they no longer believed in Norvell and his coaching staff, and there's a good case to be made that changing coaches will juice up outside spending.

But the financial reality at Florida State is ugly. Because the school had been so far behind in facilities during the Fisher and Taggart eras, Florida State needed to spend $400 million just to catch up. The debt service on those investments kicked in just when roster costs were exploding thanks to revenue sharing.

Now, on top of that, it will cost tens of millions of dollars more to swap out coaching staffs. Though Norvell's buyout number of $47 million will likely be lower than that because he has a duty to mitigate written into his contract — in other words, when Norvell gets another job, the money he's paid will be subtracted from what FSU owes him — there's still the matter of assistant coaches and staff members who have compensation guaranteed beyond this year. And, of course, there will likely be buyouts to pay to get the next coach out of his current contract. It's such an expensive proposition that Florida State's administration was desperate for Norvell to hold on at least another year so that the financials could stabilize.

Since firing Mike Alford earlier this year, Florida State's athletic department has essentially been run by Board of Trustees chairman Peter Collins. Between Collins and president Richard McCullough, there is a heavy hand in athletics from the university side but very little evidence they know what they're doing.

At a meeting of trustees this week, Collins acknowledged that the athletic director search hadn't even started yet, largely because of a top-to-bottom review of the athletic department that is expected to lead to major structural changes. While that may yield positive results over the long haul, it's unclear exactly what it means and who's going to be in charge. Perhaps there's a world where Florida State can speed run its AD search and involve that person in picking the next coach, but that's an awful lot to do in the span of four or five weeks.

While it won't matter as much for current assistants, Group of Six coaches or retreads looking for one last shot, anyone with good options will have deep concerns about the administrative structure and what kind of athletic department they're walking into.

At many points in history, the Florida State brand was strong enough that even a small leap of faith felt like a safe bet. It's harder to make that case now.

Everyone knows the Seminoles want out of the ACC and even sued the league over its restrictive grant of rights.

The good news is that a legal settlement in 2025 made it less financially penal to change conferences and led to some concessions Florida State had wanted like revenue distribution weighted to football and men's basketball TV ratings. The bad news is, nobody else wants Florida State in their league for the foreseeable future. If somehow the ACC organically broke up, it would be North Carolina and Virginia — not Florida State — in the middle of a tug-of-war between the SEC and Big Ten.

There's simply no way to predict what Florida State's future looks like five years down the road. It could be anything from trying independence to being forced to join the Big 12 because the ACC imploded to status quo to being included in a 40-team super league that breaks away from the rest of college football. That uncertainty makes it difficult to know what kind of job it will become. In some ways, FSU may not even look as attractive to some candidates as Maryland, which has very little historical success but at least has a lucrative spot in the Big Ten.

None of this means Florida State is doomed to permanent irrelevance. In the NIL/transfer portal era, college football has seen plenty of new hires have success under similar or even more difficult circumstances.

But the era of viewing Florida State as one of the sport's blue-blood jobs that can attract the interest of successful, sitting power conference coaches is essentially over. In the Bowden era, Florida State fully leveraged its geography in the state's panhandle, being easily accessible to the I-4 corridor talent hub as well as South Georgia. But now that neighborhood is ruled by the nearby SEC schools like Alabama, Georgia and Auburn, all of whom have more money to spend on players.

Selling recruits on the iconic gold helmet with the spear logo isn't enough anymore.

These limitations don't absolve Norvell from responsibility for how quickly the program slipped after 2023 when it finished the regular season 13-0. But it does mean this search will have a different tenor than the last one, when some big names were at least intrigued by the opportunity.

This time, Florida State's administration will have a lot of explaining to do with candidates about its path to success in the current era. Whether the school reaches to the past and brings back Fisher (who has made it known he wants the job) or takes a flier on an up-and-coming assistant, this will not be a star-studded candidate pool like we've seen the last couple times the job has come open.

The Seminoles were probably overdue to pull the plug on the failed Norvell era. But given the program's current situation, that's not even half the battle.

articles.title: Hernández Hernández: "Yo veo penalti claro y el VAR confirma la decisión"
articles.standfirst: El colegiado considera que no hay dudas en la decisión clave del partido
articles.summary: El colegiado considera que no hay dudas en la decisión clave del partido
articles.body: Alejandro Hernández Hernández dirigió el derbi entre Athletic y Real Sociedad y asumió la plena responsabilidad en el postpartido de DAZN tras señalar el penalti de Aramburu, la acción polémica que terminó decidiendo el derbi vasco en San Mamés. "Es un pase entre lineas. Llego bien y me pilla en la lateral y veo que es dentro. Nico hace el regate y Aramburu impacta con él de una forma que considero punible. Penalti claro", cometió el colegiado. Hernández Hernández vio como su decisión era corroborada por la sala VOR: "El VAR confirma la decisión. Tiene que ser un error claro para que actúe y desde la sala VOR se considera que no es así. Mi opinion y la de VAR difiere de la consideración de la Real". Jon Mikel Aramburu no dio crédito en directo sobre el césped de San Mamés a que Hernández Hernández señalase penalti suyo sobre Nico Williams, en una acción que terminó decidiendo el derbi, porque tenía claro que tocó el balón, como así corroboró al final del partido cuando le enseñaron la imagen en televisión. Aramburu fue preguntado al final del partido en DAZN por lo disputado del derbi. “Todos los derbis son disputados y sabíamos que iba a ser así y que se iba a decidir por detalles y ha sido con un penalti que no lo es. Me acaban de enseñar que el chip dice claramente que toqué el balón y el árbitro afirma que yo no toqué el balón, teniendo la tecnología, me parece increíble que pite un penalti así, cuando claramente toco el balón. Hasta Nico me decía que para él no era penalti; es una pena que el derbi se haya decidido por una acción polémica”. Como Aramburu, el capitán de la Real, Mikel Oyarzabal no ve penalti en la acción clave del choque: "En directo me dice que el penalti está confirmado. Que el chip confirma que no hay toque, pero las imagenes dejan claro que toca el balón". El delantero confirma que el colegiado le reiteró que no iba a cambiar su decisión: "Me dice que está confirmado por el VAR y, viendo las imágenes, el balón cambia de dirección tras el toque de Nico. En el VAR le dicen que no hay toque de Jon. Me resulta extraña, pero poco más" Por la parte del Athletic, también consideraron que el penalti era muy dudoso. El técnico de los leones, Edin Terzic, cree que fueron beneficiados en esa jugada. "Hay que recordar lo que dije otras veces. Ha habido decisiones duras en nuestra contra otras veces y nunca he dicho nada al respecto. Tampoco lo haré ahora porque no me gusta hablar de los árbitros, ni de buena ni de mala manera. Hoy tengo la sensación de que hemos sido favorecidos"

articles.title: Matarazzo: "No es penalti, Jon toca el balón, no entiendo porque el VAR no lo anuló"
articles.standfirst: El técnico de la Real se mostró muy insignado con la decisión de Hernández Hernández
articles.summary: El técnico de la Real se mostró muy insignado con la decisión de Hernández Hernández
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo se mostró indignado con la decisión del árbitro y el VAR de considerar penalti la acción entre Nico Williams y Jon Mikel Aramburu, porque en las tomas que vieron en el banquillo de la Real Sociedad tenían claro que el defensa había tocado el balón. Matarazzo tenía clara su idea sobre lo que había pasado en San Mamés. “El partido se ha decidido en un penalti donde Jon claramente toca el balón. Es muy, muy decepcionante, especialmente porque tenemos tecnología que muestra que Jon tocó el balón, Nico tocó el primero y el chip registró que Jon tocó el segundo. Para mí no es claramente un penalti y no entiendo por qué el VAR no ha intervenido y anulado el penalti, porque ese es el gol decisivo en este partido y no creo que este juego mereciera ese error como gol decisivo”. El técnico realista estaba muy contrariado por la no actuación del VAR. “¿Qué me molestó más? Sentí que ni siquiera lo comprobaron, sentí que tenían claro en unos cinco segundos que era un penalti. Eso es lo que no entiendo, porque vemos claramente en el banquillo que el balón cambia de dirección y eso es lo que más me molesta, una decisión tan decisiva no fue revisada dos veces”.

articles.title: Arsenal's 'defensive masterclass' praised in Liverpool win as Jamie Carragher salutes 'world class' Declan Rice
articles.summary: Arsenal eked out a first victory at Anfield for 14 years by beating Liverpool 1-0 thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half winner; Jamie Carragher called their defensive performance outstanding and reserved special praise for Declan Rice
articles.body:
Winning at Anfield is a rarity, especially for Arsenal. But Arteta's side were ruthless at both ends of the pitch, a tactical triumph for the boss and one that underlines his side's champion mentality.

"I love when there is something that we haven't done for many years," beamed the Spaniard, who praised his players for a defensive performance he called "remarkable". If Arteta wanted to make a statement, he succeeded.

Despite being pinned back in a first half dominated by Liverpool pressure, the visitors restricted their hosts to zero accurate shots - the first time on record the Reds failed to land at least one attempt on target at home.

"In the end, that defensive line, the way we stick together, that togetherness we have, is undefeated," midfielder Declan Rice reflected. "It's nothing I've ever seen before." Nine games in, Arsenal's title defence is going perfectly to plan.

Jamie Carragher was equally impressed by Arsenal's resilience: "To come to Anfield and be put under that much pressure and not have a shot on target from the opposition, or Liverpool not get a big chance given the money they have spent on their attack, is outstanding.

"When you think about Arsenal winning titles, especially in '89 and '91 with Tony Adams and that famous back four, I think we're getting close to putting this back four in that conversation."

Gary Neville called it a "defensive masterclass", likening Arsenal's nous to that of a side styled on Jose Mourinho's unique compactness.

The Gunners also won 18 fouls, Jurrien Timber, Martin Odegaard and Noni Madueke all responsible for drawing three apiece - a tactic used to stifle Liverpool's momentum. Ezri Konsa won all eight of the duels he contested.

Such application and exertion is what pleased Arteta most.

Under him, Arsenal have gone on to win 81 per cent of league games in which they have opened the scoring - the masters of preserving a lead.

He added: "Not only for the victory, but for the way we've done it, the spirit that we showed, the way we carried this shirt, this badge. It's a commitment of every single player in every action to deliver those kinds of stats.

"And that's the magical part about this game, that it can take you to really bad places, but four days later you have an incredible opportunity to do something historic, and we've done it."

'World-class Rice the best in Premier League'

While Carragher was impressed with the Gunners' collective effort on Super Sunday , he singled out Rice for particular commendation, calling him a "world class" talent.

The midfielder delivered one of his most complete performances of the campaign so far, providing the assist for Kai Havertz's winner and anchoring the middle third in a way that prime Arteta would be proud of.

He was the defensive shield Arsenal needed when Liverpool were generating a headwind and made crucial interceptions in the pressure moments.

His 62 touches were the most of any Arsenal player. "He's one of the best midfield players Arsenal have ever had," Carragher added.

"They've obviously had some great ones. He's right up there with the best of them. He's the best midfield player in the Premier League by a long way. It's not even a debate."

articles.title: AP Top 25: Ohio State drops nine spots after loss to USC
articles.summary: The Buckeyes fell out of the top 10.
articles.body:
Ohio State tumbled all the way out of the top 10 following its loss to USC.

The Buckeyes dropped from No. 2 to No. 11 after a 30-18 defeat to the Trojans on Saturday night. It was the first start for true freshman QB Luke Fahey after Julian Sayin injured his throwing shoulder in a win over Indiana.

Ohio State became the 11th top 10 team in the past three weeks to lose a game. Additionally, at least one team in the top two of the AP poll has lost in each of the past three weeks.

Miami stayed at No. 1 after a three-point win over North Carolina that included two onside kick recoveries nullified because of penalties. Georgia moved up to No. 2 after a dominant win over Florida, while Utah jumped three spots to No. 3 after blowing out Cincinnati on the road.

Notre Dame is at No. 4 after a win over Navy and UCLA is now at No. 5 after beating Nevada. Yes, the Bruins are really the highest-ranked team from the Big Ten.

Indiana dropped two spots to No. 6 after an overtime win over Minnesota. The Hoosiers' offense has struggled over the past four games and QB Josh Hoover was replaced by Grant Wilson after halftime. Hoover took a big hit on an interception right before the break.

The top 10 is filled out by BYU, Kentucky, Alabama and Texas.

USC moved back into the top 25 at No. 18 after the win over Ohio State. Iowa also jumped into the poll at No. 20 and New Mexico is now ranked at No. 22. The Lobos are two spots behind Boise State at No. 20 as the race for the College Football Playoff's Group of Six spot appears to be between those two teams as November begins.

articles.title: 9 options for Florida State's Next Head Coach After Mike Norvell Firing
articles.summary: To the surprise of very few, Florida State has parted ways with Mike Norvell and is currently in the market for a new football coach.
articles.body:
To the surprise of very few, Florida State has parted ways with Mike Norvell and is currently in the market for a new football coach.

Norvell will be paid handsomely to leave after leading the program for seven seasons, highlighted by a 13-1 year in 2023. But with only 10 wins over the past two-plus seasons, the momentum to move on from Norvell was building. A loss to Clemson on Saturday sealed the decision, although we've been heading this direction for some while.

The Seminoles are in desperate need of a reset and new direction. And while recent results don't exactly scream excellence, the rich football history still makes this a desired job.

As for some candidates likely to be discussed, here they are.

Let's make something abundantly clear. We don't believe this is the direction Florida State will go, nor would we encourage the program to do this in any shape or form. But given Sanders' history with the school and the conversation that has long connected the coach and his former school, it's worth noting.

A few years ago, it would have made a lot of sense.

Sanders, of course, starred at Florida State as a player. When he led Colorado to a nine-win season in 2024, many started connecting the dots.

The problem? The Buffaloes are 6-14 since, and a program that was full of life when he arrived has seemingly lost most of his juice.

The allure of Sanders is obvious. In the era of NIL and recruiting, he still has a big presence, and the connection to his former school would allow his personality to flourish.

Still, Colorado's recent performance likely dooms this possibility. His teams just haven't won enough, and Florida State can't take that chance.

Now, this would make a ton of sense. In fact, while it wouldn't be the sexiest hire possible, it could wind up being the most successful.

Some of you are probably wondering one simple question.

He's currently the head coach of Wake Forest, and he's in his second year with the school after coaching Washington State for four seasons. In his two years with the Demon Deacons, Dickert is 15-5.

In 2026, Wake Forest is 7-1 and currently No. 14 in the latest AP Poll. Again, this is Wake Forest. Since 2006, this program has won 10 or more games just once. Dickert could very well reach that figure with a strong close.

What Dickert has done exceptionally well is recruit while also finding talent in the transfer portal. Despite not operating with an enormous NIL budget, Wake Forest, which currently owns the nation's No. 9 ranked scoring offense and No. 22 ranked scoring defense, has accomplished plenty.

Again, there will be bigger names. But Dickert is a proven winner, has familiarity with the conference and could immediately make this program better.

It didn't work in Miami, and perhaps that would give some hesitation. What Diaz has done since taking over the Hurricanes, however, has been awfully impressive.

When he was hired by James Franklin to coach Penn State's defense in 2021, the Nittany Lions excelled. Diaz parlayed his success coaching defense in Happy Valley into another head coaching gig.

After winning nine games with Duke in 2024 and 2025, which included an ACC Championship last year, Diaz has coached Duke to a 5-2 mark in 2026, although games at Miami and Wake Forest are still to come.

Still, he's done an excellent job when given an opportunity, and he also attended Florida State as a student and got his start in coaching at FSU as a graduate assistant under Bobby Bowden.

He checks a lot of boxes, for certain. While the fan base might not love this one if it were ultimately the decision the school went with, Florida State could do a lot worse.

It's a matter of time for Eck, who has proven to be both a great coach and an enormous personality.

He won big at Idaho, and now he's winning big at New Mexico. In his first year with the program, Eck's team won nine games in 2025. This year, New Mexico is 7-1, with the lone loss coming against Oklahoma in a close game. As a head coach, he's 42-18.

This week, New Mexico was ranked in the Top 25 of the AP Poll for the first time with a potential trip to the CFB Playoff in sight. Oh, and the Lobos currently have the No. 1 scoring defense in the country. Not too shabby.

Away from the field, Eck is a press conference favorite and a quote machine. While he might not be a big name yet, that time is coming. And Eck's personality coupled with Florida State's resources could make for a perfect marriage.

Again, Eck will get his shot at a Power Four school. Whether it's Florida State or somewhere else, the team that ultimately lands him will be thrilled that they did.

He's never been a head coach before, and that could derail the possibility and fit altogether. With that said, Faulkner is widely recognized as one of the brightest offensive minds in all of college football, and he's likely to be a head coach sooner than later.

He helped Georgia win two national championships, albeit in a smaller role. At Georgia Tech, his first stop as an OC, his reputation took off.

Now with Florida, Faulkner still has plenty of fans despite an up-and-down Gators season. Questions and injuries at quarterback certainly haven't helped; neither has a brutal SEC schedule.

Still, if Florida State is comfortable hiring a coach with new prior experience, this would be the one. Faulkner would immediately attract top quarterbacks given his offensive background, which is something this program could desperately use.

Of course, Florida State should pursue Chesney. It absolutely has to. The question isn't whether the Seminoles would want him. It's whether he would consider leaving a place he seems to genuinely enjoy for a program that has been unstable in recent years.

Then again, that was once UCLA. Then Chesney arrived, and the Bruins are now 8-0 with the possibility of a College Football Playoff berth suddenly very real.

Wherever Chesney has gone, he's won. Before UCLA, Chesney led James Madison to the CFB Playoff. Before that, he lifted Holy Cross to back-to-back 10-win seasons.

He's still just 49-years-old, and he's likely to be the most discussed coach of this cycle. Depending on what jobs ultimately open up, Chesney will have to decide to stay at UCLA, where he is likely to get a new contract and an enormous raise, or leave for another place.

Florida State has to try. In fact, it should do everything it can, which includes offering an enormous sum of money for him, his coaching staff and an NIL budget, to make it possible.

With a big buyout for Norvell on deck, however, the whole fit feels unlikely. That said, FSU would be foolish not to swing big. He's that good.

Weird? Absolutely. Impossible? Maybe not. Florida State won a national title under Fisher, who has been out of work for a few years after being fired by Texas A&M. If financial considerations are apart of this process, FSU could probably hire Fisher for a lot less than most of the other coaches on this list. We don't see it happening, but you never know.

He loves Arizona State, although he did flirt with the Michigan job this past offseason. it hasn't exactly gone great with the Sun Devils this fall, although that shouldn't deter any interest Florida State might have. It could, however, prompt Dillingham to look at his current gig and reconsider leaving a place he clearly cares greatly about.

Given how things ended at LSU, it's hard to know how Florida State would feel about the possibility. It's even harder to know how Florida State fans would take this one also. Still, Kelly has won big, coached at major programs and won a lot of football games. He also seems eager to get back on the sideline, which makes this an interesting connection.

articles.title: Bianchi: FSU fires Mike Norvell, but downfall began when playoff committee robbed him of his mojo
articles.summary: Mike Norvell was fired as Florida State’s football coach Sunday, but I believe he actually lost his job nearly three years ago. On Dec. 3, 2023, to be exact....
articles.body:
Mike Norvell was fired as Florida State's football coach Sunday, but I believe he actually lost his job nearly three years ago. On Dec. 3, 2023, to be exact.

That was the day the College Football Playoff selection committee robbed his undefeated Seminoles of an opportunity to compete for a national championship. That was the day everything Norvell had preached to his players about hard work, sacrifice and winning suddenly rang hollow. And that was the day something inside Mike Norvell seemed to die as well.

I can still see the look on his face. Devastation. Disbelief. Betrayal. It was the look of a man who had just discovered that everything he believed about college football was a lie.

His Seminoles had done everything he'd asked. They had worked. They had sacrificed. They had overcome adversity. They had won every single game, including the ACC championship. Thirteen games. Thirteen victories. Zero losses. And their reward? A swift kick in the teeth from the College Football Playoff selection committee.

The committee inexplicably left undefeated Florida State out of the four-team playoff, choosing one-loss Alabama instead. It was the only time an undefeated Power Four team had been left out of the playoff. The justification was that the Seminoles weren't the same team without injured quarterback Jordan Travis.

Imagine explaining that to a locker room full of young men who had spent an entire year believing their coach's most sacred promise: Do your job. Win your games. Take care of your business. And you'll get your opportunity to compete for a national championship.

The committee didn't just steal Florida State's championship opportunity that day. It stole something from Mike Norvell, too. His belief. His confidence. His mojo. And, looking back now, I don't think he ever got it back.

Norvell's firing Sunday came after another humiliating defeat, this one a 36-24 home loss to a mediocre Clemson team. His final record: 41-39 over nearly seven seasons. But the most damning statistic is this: Since that glorious 13-0 season ended in heartbreak, Florida State has gone an unfathomable 10-23.

Think about that. The coach who couldn't lose suddenly couldn't win. The offensive mastermind seemingly forgot how to call plays. The quarterback whisperer couldn't find a quarterback. The talent evaluator who once worked the transfer portal like a Wall Street wizard suddenly seemed incapable of distinguishing a difference-maker from a benchwarmer.

How does that happen? How does a coach who seemingly had all the answers suddenly find himself with none? Maybe the explanation is simpler than we want to believe. Maybe Mike Norvell was never the same after the day college football broke his heart.

The first indication came weeks after the playoff snub, when more than 20 Seminoles opted out of the Orange Bowl or entered the transfer portal. The result was a 63-3 annihilation by Georgia — the most lopsided result in the history of bowl games. It wasn't a football game. It was a nationally televised funeral for everything Florida State had built. And the corpse never quite came back to life.

The Seminoles went 2-10 in 2024, 5-7 last season and were 3-5 this season when the university finally decided enough was enough.

To be fair, Norvell wasn't the only one who failed. Florida State's administration was painfully slow to recognize that college football had become a billionaire's auction house, where NIL money and the transfer portal had turned roster building into an arms race. The Seminoles sometimes looked like a Blockbuster manager trying to figure out why everybody was suddenly watching Netflix.

Eventually, FSU opened its wallet and moths flew out, but by then the damage had been done. Even increased spending couldn't fix the quarterback failures, personnel mistakes and coaching shortcomings.

And let's not forget the colossal miscalculation by former athletic director Michael Alford, who rewarded Norvell with a massive contract extension after the 2023 season. At the time, it seemed perfectly reasonable. Who knew Florida State was paying filet mignon prices for a coach who was about to start serving gas-station hot dogs? That decision left the financially strained athletic department staring at a buyout of roughly $50 million.

Which is why Florida State deserves some credit for giving Norvell every conceivable opportunity to resurrect his career. The university invested more resources. Revamped personnel operations. Swallowed embarrassing losses. Endured the outrage of an increasingly furious fan base.

All Norvell had to do Saturday was beat a beatable Clemson team at home, then navigate a remaining schedule filled with winnable games. Instead, predictably, the Seminoles lost again.

Before kickoff Saturday night, some disgruntled fan even hired a plane to circle Doak Campbell Stadium carrying a banner demanding that FSU "Fire Novell." Good grief. The poor guy couldn't even get fired with his name spelled correctly. By the fourth quarter, much of the stadium had emptied. And by Sunday, Norvell was unemployed.

There will be those who insist the playoff snub is merely a convenient excuse for a coach who stopped recruiting effectively, stopped developing quarterbacks and stopped winning football games. They're not entirely wrong. Norvell must own his failures.

But I keep coming back to that Sunday in December 2023. That stunned expression. That crushed spirit. That realization that the rules he had preached to his players apparently didn't apply when television ratings, conference politics and committee opinions entered the equation.

Perhaps the cruelest irony is that Norvell spent the next three seasons trying desperately to prove he was still the coach who had built that undefeated team. Instead, every defeat made him look more like a desperate man chasing a ghost.

Mike Norvell will leave Florida State with tens of millions of dollars, a battered reputation and the haunting memory of what might have been. He'll have plenty of time to contemplate the mistakes that cost him his job, from the quarterbacks he recruited to the games he inexplicably lost.

But I wonder whether he'll ever stop thinking about Dec. 3, 2023. About that undefeated team. About the championship opportunity that was taken away. About the promise he made to his players that winning every game would be enough.

Because in the end, the cruelest part of Norvell's downfall isn't so much that he forgot how to win.

It's that he never recovered from the cruel injustice of discovering that sometimes winning isn't enough.

Email me at mbianchi@orlandosentinel.com . Hit me up on social media @BianchiWrites and listen to my radio show "Game On" every weekday from 3 to 6 p.m. on FM 96.9, AM 740 and 969TheGame.com/listen .

articles.title: Las Vegas Raiders’ playoff standing gets a boost with Week 8 results
articles.summary: Silver and Black helped their cause and got some help on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders managed to end their four-game losing streak in Week 8 against the New York Jets , evening out their record at 4-4 and keeping their slim postseason hopes alive. Additionally, the Raiders got some help on Sunday, as we take a look at the AFC Playoff picture below.

[Editor's note: The standings below are before the second slate of Sunday's games and Sunday Night Football has completed. Silver and Black Pride will continue to update this article as the games end and standings change.]

5. Denver Broncos 5-2 (Strength of victory tiebreaker over CIN)

9. Las Vegas Raiders 4-4 (3-3 in AFC for tiebreaker over BAL)

12. New York Jets 2-6 (2-3 in AFC for tiebreaker over IND)

The Raiders got help from the Bills, who took down the Ravens 36-10. But the bigger storyline is that Baltimore could be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for the rest of the season after Jackson suffered a thumb injury that will place him on injured reserve and require surgery. The Ravens also had backup quarterback Tyler Huntley go down in the game, leaving them with a lot of question marks at the most important position on the field.

That could remove one more team from being "in the hunt", but Las Vegas still has some work to do. The Titans almost did the Silver and Black a favor, narrowly losing to the Cincinnati Bengals. But the Bengals managed to avoid the upset and climb up to the second AFC Wild Card spot, putting another AFC North team in the seventh seed: The Browns.

Las Vegas heads to Cleveland at the end of the month, but first has a matchup in San Francisco next Sunday. Meanwhile, the Browns will be in New Orleans, the Patriots host the Packers, and the Ravens take on the Jaguars this Thursday.

articles.title: 🎥 Grêmio take healthy lead in bid for Copa do Brasil final
articles.summary: Playing in front of 50,928 fans at a rocking Arena, Grêmio took a strong step toward reaching their tenth Copa do Brasil final.Thanks to goals from Carlos Vi...
articles.body:
Playing in front of 50,928 fans at a rocking Arena, Grêmio took a strong step toward reaching their tenth Copa do Brasil final.

Thanks to goals from Carlos Vinícius and Noriega (and a superb performance from Weverton), the Tricolor beat Atlético Mineiro 2–0 on Sunday (1).

It was the first leg of the competition's semi-final.

Weverton steals the show in the first half

Cuello had a great chance to put Atlético ahead.

But he could not beat the Grêmio goalkeeper.

Weverton would make another decisive contribution moments later.

His goal kick turned into an assist for Carlos Vinícius, who capitalised on a mistake by Lyanco to score (11').

The man behind the assist got plenty of love in the celebrations.

Atlético went into the break having dominated possession (over 70%).

Grêmio extend their lead as Galo push forward

It was a dream start to the second half for the Tricolor.

Just two minutes in, a fine move down the right ended with Noriega scoring.

With no other option, Barba Domínguez made Galo increasingly attack-minded.

Even youngster Cauã Soares, an out-and-out centre-forward, was brought on.

And their big chance came in the 94th minute, when Vitor Hugo rattled the crossbar.

Gustavo Martins left the Tricolor down to ten men shortly afterwards.

But Galo had no time to make the most of their numerical advantage.

The return leg takes place next Saturday (7) at Arena MRV.

Grêmio can afford to lose by one goal and still reach the final.

Galo, meanwhile, will need to win by three goals in front of their home fans to go through in normal time.

A two-goal win would send the tie to penalties.

Both teams now turn their attention back to the Brasileirão. And both head to Rio de Janeiro.

Sitting 15th after two straight wins, Grêmio face leaders Flamengo at the Maracanã.

Galo, who have lost their last two league matches, are seventh and will face Botafogo (12th) at the Nilton Santos.

Both matches take place next Wednesday (4).

articles.title: Player Ratings: Racing Santander 0–3 Real Madrid
articles.summary: Thibaut Courtois: 8. Only had to make one save, but it was an outstanding intervention to preserve the clean sheet. Trent Alexander-Arnold: 7. A quiet night...
articles.body:
Thibaut Courtois: 8. Only had to make one save, but it was an outstanding intervention to preserve the clean sheet.

Trent Alexander-Arnold: 7. A quiet night statistically, but his advanced positioning consistently gave Bellingham, Güler, and Mbappé a valuable outlet on the right. Helped create several effective overloads.

Ibrahima Konaté: 7. Had relatively little defensive work to do, with most of Racing's attacks coming down the opposite side. Solid on the ball throughout.

Dean Huijsen: 8.5. Tremendous on the ball again. Played the vital pass out of Racing's press in the build-up to Bellingham's goal. Also recorded seven clearances and four blocked shots, including two crucial interventions — one in each half.

Marc Cucurella: 8. Completely shut down Luque, Mantilla, and whoever else attacked his flank. Finished with four clearances, four tackles, and four interceptions in an excellent defensive display.

Bernardo Silva: 6.5. Not his cleanest passing performance, and he switched off on a couple of occasions. Responded well at the start of the second half, however, when Racing began pressing more aggressively.

Aurélien Tchouaméni: 7.5. Strong in his challenges and excellent at reading passing lanes. His six interceptions reflected how well he anticipated Racing's attempts to move the ball forward.

Arda Güler: 8.5. A superb performance. Created six key passes — five in the first half — and registered an assist while completing 97.5% of his passes, including all eight long balls. Unfortunately, his shooting opportunities fell to his right foot; otherwise, he might well have added a goal.

Jude Bellingham: 8.5. He's on a roll. His off-ball run and finish for Real Madrid's second goal were perfectly executed. His link-up play, pressing, and distribution in tight spaces were all excellent.

Yan Diomande: 8.5. Unstoppable dribbling, dangerous link-up play, outstanding defensive work, and a golazo. A tremendous two-way performance.

Kylian Mbappé: 8.5. Thriving with this supporting cast. Made excellent off-ball runs, combined with teammates across the pitch, and opened the scoring. His hold-up play in the build-up to Bellingham's goal was another highlight.

Brahim Díaz: 6.5. A relatively quiet cameo. Had just 18 touches and often went without service when he made runs.

Eduardo Camavinga: 6.5. Also relatively quiet, though he showed good ball-carrying and distribution during his time on the pitch.

Endrick: N/A. Nearly scored with an excellent effort from outside the box.

articles.title: Pepe Mel, en la UCI tras ser operado de un ictus en Sevilla
articles.standfirst: El exentrenador del Betis, Rayo, Málaga o Dépor, entre otros, permanece ingresado en observación
articles.summary: El exentrenador del Betis, Rayo, Málaga o Dépor, entre otros, permanece ingresado en observación
articles.body: Pepe Mel fue operado con éxito en Sevilla tras sufrir un accidente cerebrovascular el 1 de noviembre. El técnico madrileño, de 63 años, permanece ingresado en la UCI de un hospital de la ciudad, donde seguirá bajo observación durante las próximas horas, según fuentes cercanas al Real Betis y a su entorno. Hasta el momento no se ha difundido ningún parte médico oficial. La noticia ha golpeado de lleno al beticismo. Mel conoce el club desde dentro, ya que fue delantero verdiblanco (Pichichi de Segunda en la 89-90), lo entrenó en dos etapas y en una de ellas lo devolvió a Primera División. Vive en Sevilla desde hace años y, desde que se conoció su ingreso, las redes sociales se han llenado de mensajes de cariño y ánimo de aficionados, compañeros y clubes. Su recorrido en los banquillos ha pasado por Murcia, Tenerife, Getafe, Alavés, Rayo Vallecano, Deportivo, Las Palmas, Málaga y Almería, equipo al que dirigió en las diez últimas jornadas de la temporada 2024-25. Además, dirigió en el extranjero. En la actualidad no tiene equipo. Queda por conocer el parte médico oficial y la evolución de los próximos días. Hasta entonces, el Betis y todos los equipos por los que ha pasado esperan noticias de un entrenador que, en Sevilla, nunca ha dejado de ser de casa.

articles.title: Un penaltito averió el partido
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Quince años hacía que el Madrid no visitaba al Racing, un clásico de nuestro fútbol, y el reencuentro se produjo en una tarde otoñal reventona, con cielo abierto y brisa agradable. El césped, perfecto, invitaba al buen juego y el Madrid, que venía con el impulso del Spotify y la misma alineación salvo el descanso preventivo de Valverde, salió con ganas y alegría atacante. El Racing, un equipo mejor por delante que por detrás como bien se lee en sus resultados (el curso pasado ascendió a Primera con más goles encajados que el Zaragoza, que descendió), reculó asustado. Cuando se te echa encima un Madrid con tantas ganas y esos tremendos atacantes, es para asustarse. Y el gol se masticaba desde el principio. La lástima fue que, tras algunas ocasiones perdidas, llegó con un penalti-penaltito, un penalti-pigmeo, mitad de cuarto de penalti si me mide en la romana. Mbappé puso más de sí que Prati. Munuera Montero tuvo un instante de duda, pero pitó, y los requerimientos de los racinguistas no le conmovieron, ni el VAR, desde su cómoda distancia en Las Rozas, vio oportuno convocarle a la pantalla. Consecuencia: gol del propio Mbappé, el partido ya en cuesta abajo para el Madrid y un público irritado que se expresó con los gritos de ritual “¡Así, así gana el Madrid!”, que nació cerca de aquí, en El Molinón, en los lejanos ochenta y el “¡Fuera Tebas!”, contradictoriamente incubado en el Bernabéu, donde complace echar a este hombre la culpa de todo. El Madrid estaba jugando muy bien y una vez que el Racing tuvo que moverse algo más casi puede decirse que abusó. Tuvo contraataques escalofriantes y alcanzó con facilidad el 0-3, vía Bellingham, cuyo primer tiempo fue soberbio, y Diomande, con una volea tremenda a la salida de un córner. Aparte de otras virtudes (regate, trabajo, ingenio…) tiene disparo. Con 0-3, claro, todo estaba resuelto. Una vez un periodista le preguntó a Di Stéfano si era mejor el 4-3-3 o el 4-4-2, y él contestó que la única táctica buena era el “un, dos, tres y descansar, y si te meten uno, meter el cuarto.” Así volvimos al segundo tiempo, con el Madrid esperando que el Racing le metiera uno para desperezarse, pero no se dio pese a que durante un cuarto de hora lució el buen estilo de su ataque. Pudo llegar en una mano de Tchouaméni de la que el linier avisó a Munuera, que pitó penalti, pero esta vez sí le llamó el VAR, lo revisó y lo echó para atrás, para mayor enfado del público. Y así se fue por el desagüe un partido que pintaba para bueno, pero que un penalti-pigmeo averió. El Atlético fue líder ayer durante siete horas y media, entre el final de su victoria en el Ciutat de Valencia y la del Barça en el Camp Nou. Parece poco, pero me ha traído al recuerdo aquella película ‘Treinta segundos sobre Tokio’, con Spencer Tracy en el papel de Doolittle en su arriesgada operación de bombardeo a la capital nipona. Fue sólo un golpe de efecto pero anunciaba algo. En estas horas el Atlético ha recordado que LaLiga no es cosa de dos. Y el domingo espera al Barça… El Rayo pudo jugar un partido en paz en su campo y lo ganó. Pero no es lo mismo paz que armonía. Las dos partes si se puede decir así, porque una es la propiedad, o sea Presa, y la otra todo el barrio, han pactado una tregua que la plantilla, torturada con lo que estaba ocurriendo, agradeció con una bonita victoria ante el Celta, 3-0. Aún se arrastra el estropicio del Rayo-Athletic, pero de momento el equipo se estabiliza en la tabla. Pero la pipa de la paz no se ha fumado.

articles.title: Studs and duds from Commanders' big win over Eagles
articles.summary: The Commanders took down the Eagles on Sunday night, so let's see who impressed and who didn't.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders had the chance to host Sunday Night Football against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 8.

This was a crucial matchup for the Commanders as they entered this week with just one win. The NFC East is still wide open, though, so every win matters. Well, luckily, the Commanders were able to get that elusive second win of the season.

The Eagles won the first quarter, scoring 10 points, but that was the only offense the team could generate. The Commanders would end up winning 27-10, and there were plenty of solid performances on both sides of the ball. Now, let's identify our biggest studs and duds.

Entering this game, it seemed like the Commanders should be able to run the ball . The Eagles have given up a ton of yardage on the ground this season, so this seemed like the perfect get-right game.

Rachaad White delivered, rushing for 55 yards and one touchdown on 11 carries. White had the game-sealing run in the fourth quarter and then punched it in for his first rushing score of the season. The free agent addition delivered when it mattered.

Chig Okonkwo played a big role the last time the Commanders were on the field. With Terry McLaurin out, it really seemed like Okonkwo would get a ton of targets going forward.

Well, against the Eagles, Okonkwo didn't have his finest moment. The veteran caught two passes for 32 yards on four targets, and also lost a fumble. The Commanders will need more from Okonkwo going forward. Most will forget his overall lack of production, though as he made a spectacular one-handed grab in the third quarter.

Treylon Burks is another player who should get more opportunities with McLaurin out. The former first-round pick made the most of his chances on Sunday, leading the team with 81 receiving yards.

Burks had three catches, including a 53-yarder, and showed that he can be a reliable option for Jayden Daniels.

Next up, the entire defensive front needs to be shouted out. The Commanders racked up five sacks, eight tackles for loss, and nine quarterback hits. The unit dominated the banged-up Eagles' offensive line and showed what it can be on a good day.

Dorance Armstrong, Shy Tuttle, K'Lavon Chaisson, Charles Omenihu, and Odafe Oweh each recorded a sack. And they did this without starters Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw.

We mentioned Rachaad White having the game-sealing play on offense; well, Rasul Douglas had the game-sealing play on defense. The Eagles were trailing 19-10 and were technically still alive when Tanner McKee threw a deep pass intended for Darius Cooper.

Rasul Douglas came up with the interception, and then White busted off his long run. It was a nice play for Douglas in an otherwise inconsistent season.

articles.title: El Kane de Oro que llega a Madrid: nuevas 'armas'... y un desafío
articles.standfirst: El Balón de Oro estrena botas en el Metropolitano... donde perdió una final de Champions
articles.summary: El Balón de Oro estrena botas en el Metropolitano... donde perdió una final de Champions
articles.body: El nuevo Balón de Oro, Harry Kane, estará el martes en el Metropolitano con la espinita del partido del sábado ante el Dortmund (falló un penalti e hizo dos postes) y con la mayor espinita aún de regresar a un Metropolitano en el que perdió la final de la Champions 18-19 con el Tottenham y ante el Liverpool (0-2). Hace poco, en una entrevista con MARCA, Harry nos decía esto sobre el partido del martes: "Creo que nunca he jugado contra el Atlético, será mi primera vez. Ellos han demostrado lo buenos que pueden ser. Llegaron a semis la pasada Champions, y tienen todo mi respeto. Será un partido difícil pero estamos preparados. En el Metropolitano perdí una final de Champions y fue un momento duro. Espero regresar y tener una historia diferente". Para conmemorar la Bota de Oro, Skechers Fútbol, la marca que viste y calza al inglés, estrenó el pasado sábado unas nuevas botas, con detalles en color oro, que serán las que use en Madrid. La campaña fue anunciada con el cortometraje 'Mark of Greatness’ en el que se celebraba tanto la gesta deportiva del delantero como su camino hasta aquí. Presentaba a un misterioso artesano que ha pasado años en absoluta soledad perfeccionando un anillo único dentro de un taller. Un anillo de oro que sirve a la marca para presentar esta exclusiva tirada de 73 pares de botas, uno por cada gol marcado en la temporada 2025-26 que le valieron la Bota de Oro y el Balón de Oro. Eso sí, el ejemplar para Kane es un par único para su uso personal, recubierto con auténtica hoja de oro de 24 quilates. El Kane Balón de Oro ha provocado otras iniciativas alrededor del mundo, como es el caso del cuadro gigante que le ha terminado el artista español Michel Díaz, autor de una obra cuyo título es 'El abrazo del ángel'. Un cuadro de unas medidas de 1,80 x 1,20 cm .cuya técnica es oleo y acrílico. Esto nos dice Míchel: "Me vi inspirado a pintar a Kane por su gran evolución a través de lucha y el foco que le hizo pasar de ser un gran jugador a ser un jugador top". El cuadro le será entrenado en breve. Stefan Kastner, propietario del restaurante muniqués Waldgasthof Buchenhain, hizo una promesa en septiembre y ahora ha cumplido su palabra y le ha entregado a Harry Kane cuatro schnitzel (escalopes vieneses de ternera) cubiertos de oro comestible, como se ven en la imagen. Pero ahí no termina la cosa. Hay otro reto: marcar 40 goles esta temporada en la Bundesliga. Si HK lo consigue, Stefan se compromete a esto: "Organizaremos una fiesta en el jardín para 500 personas con cerveza Hofbräu gratis y miniescalopes dorados para todos". ¿Lo conseguirá Harry?

articles.title: Mike Tomlin hits Cowboys with brutally honest reality check after Cardinals game
articles.summary: Coach Brian Schottenheimer’s Dallas Cowboys fell to 3-5 with a 33-30 overtime, home loss to the caused the Cowboys coach to speak about personal responsibili...
articles.body:
Coach Brian Schottenheimer 's Dallas Cowboys fell to 3-5 with a 33-30 overtime, home loss to the caused the Cowboys coach to speak about personal responsibility . Quarterback Dak Prescott attempted to shield his head coach from criticism afterward, but Mike Tomlin entered the fray with criticisms of his own as he spoke on Sunday Night Football later on in the night.

Ari Meirov shared Tomlin's comments, which were not sugarcoated as he tore into the Cowboys.

"I saw a bunch of blinkers, and what I mean by that, if you're a blinker, cut your eyelids off. What I mean is, you gotta relish the thick moments, you gotta want to make the play, as an individual or particular units that wanted to grab the bull by the horns and win the game. Certainly their defense, we can spend a lot of time talking about that two-minute drive and things of that nature, but their offense had a short field when they had an unsuccessful onside kick at the end of regulation, and then they went three-and-out in overtime, and so I see a team that doesn't have anybody that wants to be the unit to secure victory, they gotta cut their eyelids off."

The Cowboys lost tight end Jake Ferguson early in the game which led to a sub-200 yard passing day from QB Dak Prescott. Javonte Williams led the running game with 56 yards but it wasn't enough to inspire much hope, on a day that saw a NSFW explosion by Cowboys owner Jerry Jones .

Tomlin's words were harsh in nature, but seemed fitting given the Cowboys' latest collapse. At 3-5, they have a chance to make a run in a mediocre NFC East division, but likely won't be anyone's choice to make noise in the playoffs, if they make it that far.

articles.title: Un dilema con el Cuti Romero
articles.standfirst: ​El argentino fue el único de los suplentes en el Ciutat que no se entrenó sobre el verde en el ensayo post Levante. La duda: que sea el 'antiKane' frente al Bayern o reservarlo para el Barça
articles.summary: El argentino fue el único de los suplentes en el Ciutat que no se entrenó sobre el verde en el ensayo post Levante. La duda: que sea el 'antiKane' frente al Bayern o reservarlo para el Barça
articles.body: Garantizar a un 'antiKane' frente al Bayern o reservarlo para que afronte en plenitud la visita de los Raphinha, Lamine y compañía en la que el Atlético puede asaltar el liderato. Ese es el dilema que ronda en el Atlético después de que el Cuti Romero, su gran baluarte defensivo, no saltara al verde junto al resto de suplentes frente al Levante en el entrenamiento de este pasado domingo. Fue el único de los que no jugaron de inicio en el Ciutat de Valencia que no participó en la sesión de campo. Aunque el argentino viajó a Valencia como gran novedad de la lista después de superar la lesión de bajo grado que se produjo en el aductor frente al Espanyol y que le privó de medirse al Stuttgart y Deportivo, finalmente viviría el triunfo contra el cuadro granota desde el banquillo. Cumplía exactamente los 12 días mínimos que se estimaban para su recibir su alta médica, pero a sus 28 años y tras una carrera llena de sacrificios para acortar los plazos de recuperación en sus lesiones musculares se entendía que no era necesario forzar. Más aún teniendo en cuenta lo que se viene al Atlético en los próximos siete días en que el Bayern y el Barcelona se suceden por el Metropolitano. Sin embargo, el trabajo del Cuti este domingo en el gimnasio junto a los titulares del sábado y no en compañía de los Sorloth, Lookman, Le Normand, Jonathan David, Koke, Arnau Ortiz, Vargas, Mendoza, Domínguez y Dani Martínez sigue alimentando la duda sobre su concurso esta semana. Con Romero disponible como ya quedó patente con su convocatoria para el Levante pero aún sin el fondo como para afrontar dos partidos de tal exigencia, el dilema estriba en adelantar su concurso en la Champions o en esperar para la competición doméstica. Dicho de otro modo, la titularidad del Cuti frente al Bayern supondría una garantía para frenar al actual Balón de Oro, al que conoce como pocos tras compartir vestuario en el Tottenham y al que ya ató en corto en el pasado Mundial, pero llegaría al siguiente duelo capital ante el Barcelona con una carga extra importante. Una cuestión, en definitiva, de medir los esfuerzos... y los riesgos.

articles.title: Un golazo de Messi pone segundo al Inter Miami y le clasifica para la 'Concachampions'
articles.standfirst: Remontada de los del Kily González
articles.summary: Remontada de los del Kily González
articles.body: Leo Messi impulsó este domingo la remontada del Inter Miami ante el New England Revolution (1-2), con una asistencia y el gol decisivo, para situar a su equipo segundo de la Conferencia Este y clasificarlo para la Copa de Campeones de la Concacaf. Messi decidió el encuentro en el minuto 83 con un disparo cruzado de zurda, después de recibir un pase del venezolano Telasco Segovia. El argentino alcanzó los 26 goles en esta temporada de la MLS. La cuenta de Inter Miami en X definió así el gol: "Otro momento de magia de Messi". Antes había propiciado el empate del mexicano Germán Berterame, que marcó de cabeza en el minuto 69 y neutralizó la ventaja conseguida por el húngaro Dániel Gazdag en el 53. El Inter Miami reaccionó después de llegar al descanso sin goles y verse por detrás en un enfrentamiento directo por la segunda plaza. La victoria le permitió alcanzar los 59 puntos y superar a New England, que se quedó con 58. El conjunto de Florida cortó además una racha de dos partidos sin ganar y aseguró su participación en la próxima edición de la 'ConcaChampions', el último gran trofeo que busca Messi. La segunda posición de la conferencia todavía se decidirá en la última jornada de la fase regular, prevista para la próxima semana. El Inter Miami, con un punto de ventaja sobre New England, cerrará ante Charlotte, mientras que el Revolution se enfrentará a Orlando City.
